newsitem.title: USA: Crown Books reports quarterly loss.
newsitem.headline: Crown Books reports quarterly loss.

text.p: Crown Books Corp. reported a loss in the second quarter, as the company closed eight regular book stores and opened six new superstores.

The Landover, Md.-based company had net a loss of $1.5 million, or 28 cents per share, in the quarter ended Aug. 3. It had profits of $250,000, or 5 cents per share, in the same period last year, after $4 million of a previous provision was reversed.
However, Crown Books' operating losses shrank to $2.6 million from $3.6 million.

"Significantly narrowing our second quarter operating loss is a clear indication that our repositioning strategy is meeting our expectations," said Steve Stevens, president and chief executive officer.
Sales rose 4 percent to $66.5 million from $63.9 million.
Comparable sales for stores open more than 13 months increased 1 percent compared to the same period one year ago. Comparable sales for all superstores also edged up 1 percent.

Crown Books operates 166 book stores, including 95 Super Crown stores, in the Washington D.C. metropolitan area; California; Houston, Chicago, and Seattle, compared with 179 stores, including 74 Super Crown stores, in operation one year ago.
Crown Books' stock was unchanged at $11 on Nasdaq.
